svg.title: A curvature coordinate is a difference of two elementary edge stencils. Its two-point form consequently has four terms, with signs +, −, −, +. Both its finite-torus covariance and its infinite- cover subtraction have exactly this four-term expansion. At separated positions, (PT24) reduces each torus term to the scalar differentiated-kernel limit. At inversion-image positions it reduces each term to the scalar far-distance limit, which is zero. At coincident positions subtract the infinite-cover value before rescaling. The torus-to-cover return estimate makes this difference tend to zero even after multiplication by any fixed inverse power of h, because Nmhq m →∞for every fixed q. These are respectively the separated, far-image, and return scalar estimates needed by the chart argument.
